# hypothesis-graphql [![Build](https://github.com/Stranger6667/hypothesis-graphql/workflows/build/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Stranger6667/hypothesis-graphql/actions) [![Coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/Stranger6667/hypothesis-graphql/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/Stranger6667/hypothesis-graphql/branch/master) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/hypothesis-graphql.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/hypothesis-graphql/) [![Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/hypothesis-graphql.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/hypothesis-graphql/) [![Chat](https://img.shields.io/discord/938139740912369755)](https://discord.gg/R9ASRAmHnA) [![License](https://img.shields.io/pypi/l/hypothesis-graphql.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

Generate GraphQL queries from your schema and test your server with them

`hypothesis-graphql` gives you [Hypothesis](https://github.com/HypothesisWorks/hypothesis/tree/master/hypothesis-python) strategies that build queries and mutations from a GraphQL schema. Each generated operation selects a random subset of fields at random depth and fills arguments with random values. For a ready-made tool, try [Schemathesis](https://github.com/schemathesis/schemathesis): it runs on top of this library and reports server crashes without any test code. ## Usage `from_schema` takes a schema and returns a strategy that yields queries and mutations as strings: ```python from hypothesis import given from hypothesis_graphql import from_schema import requests # A schema string or a `graphql.GraphQLSchema` instance SCHEMA = """ type Book { title: String author: Author } type Author { name: String books: [Book] } type Query { getBooks: [Book] getAuthors: [Author] } type Mutation { addBook(title: String!, author: String!): Book! addAuthor(name: String!): Author! } """ @given(from_schema(SCHEMA)) def test_graphql(query): # Generates operations like: # # { # getBooks { # title # } # } # # mutation { # addBook(title: "H4Z\u7869", author: "\u00d2"){ # title # } # } response = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1/graphql", json={"query": query}) assert response.status_code == 200 assert response.json().get("errors") is None ``` To generate only one kind of operation, use `hypothesis_graphql.queries` or `hypothesis_graphql.mutations`. ### Customization Pass `fields` to limit which root fields appear in generated operations: ```python @given(from_schema(SCHEMA, fields=["getAuthors"])) def test_graphql(query): # Only `getAuthors` will be generated ... ``` Two arguments control generated strings: - `allow_x00` (default `True`): set it to `False` to keep `\x00` out of strings. Some web servers reject requests that contain it. - `codec` (default `utf-8`): generated strings only contain characters this codec can encode. Use `"ascii"` to stay in the ASCII range. ```python @given(from_schema(SCHEMA, allow_x00=False, codec="ascii")) def test_graphql(query): assert "\0" not in query query.encode("ascii") ``` Set `allow_null=False` to keep `null` out of argument values, including nested input fields and list items. Built-in scalars (`Int`, `Float`, `String`, `ID`, `Boolean`) work out of the box. For a custom scalar such as `Date`, pass a strategy that generates AST nodes for it: ```python from hypothesis import strategies as st, given from hypothesis_graphql import from_schema, nodes SCHEMA = """ scalar Date type Query { getByDate(created: Date!): Int } """ @given( from_schema( SCHEMA, custom_scalars={"Date": st.dates().map(nodes.String)}, ) ) def test_graphql(query): # Example: # # { getByDate(created: "2000-01-01") } # ... ``` Without a strategy, `hypothesis-graphql` skips optional arguments of that type and raises `hypothesis.errors.InvalidArgument` if a required argument uses it. `hypothesis_graphql.nodes` has helpers that build value nodes: - `String` -> `graphql.StringValueNode` (converts the value with `str()`) - `Float` -> `graphql.FloatValueNode` - `Int` -> `graphql.IntValueNode` - `Object` -> `graphql.ObjectValueNode` - `List` -> `graphql.ListValueNode` - `Boolean` -> `graphql.BooleanValueNode` - `Enum` -> `graphql.EnumValueNode` - `Null` -> `graphql.NullValueNode` (a constant, not a function) Use them in `map` calls: `graphql.StringValueNode` and friends accept keyword arguments only. ### Negative Testing Pass `mode=Mode.NEGATIVE` to generate operations your server must reject: ```python from hypothesis import given from hypothesis_graphql import queries, Mode import requests SCHEMA = """ type Query { getUser(id: Int!, name: String!): User } type User { id: Int! name: String! } """ @given(queries(SCHEMA, mode=Mode.NEGATIVE)) def test_server_rejects_invalid_queries(query): # Each query violates the schema in exactly one of these ways: # - a value of the wrong type (a string for an `Int`) # - a missing required argument # - an `Int` outside the 32-bit range # - `null` for a non-null argument # - an unknown enum value # - an input object without one of its required fields response = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1/graphql", json={"query": query}) # The server must answer with an error status or an `errors` list if response.status_code == 200: assert "errors" in response.json() ``` `queries`, `mutations`, and `from_schema` all accept `mode`. If no argument in the schema allows any of these violations, negative mode raises `InvalidArgument`. ## License `hypothesis-graphql` is available under the [MIT license](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT). By contributing, you agree to license your contributions under it.
